descripcion_geo: Desert camp whose name means 'graves of desire/greed'; place where Israel was punished for lusting after meat.
importancia_estrategica: Desert camp: the graves of those who desired meat.

historias.titulo: The people crave meat in Kibrot-hataavah
historias.descripcion: Israel cries for meat; God sends quails in abundance but strikes the people with a great plague while the meat was still between their teeth.

historias.titulo: The Spirit upon the seventy elders at Kibrot-hataavah
historias.descripcion: In the same camp, God extends the Spirit that was upon Moses upon the seventy elders; Eldad and Medad prophesy.

historias.titulo: The name as a memorial of sin
historias.descripcion: The place was called Kibrot-hataava ('graves of desire') because those they had coveted were buried there.

personajes.descripcion: He interceded for the people exhausted by the burden and received the promise of the seventy elders of the Spirit.
He asked Moses to silence Eldad and Medad; Moses replied: 'If only all of God's people would prophesy!'
They prophesied in the camp although they had not approached the tent; They received the Spirit just like the seventy.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Kibrot-hataava: relevant geographical region in the Old Testament.

judaismo.descripcion: Kibrot-hataava memorializes the danger of greed: Israel received what he asked for but paid a high price; Uncontrolled desire leads to death.
judaismo.significado_teologico: Kibrot-hataava memorializes the danger of greed: Israel received what he asked for but paid a high price; Uncontrolled desire leads to death.
